key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search identified 58 CuI-based ternary compounds as promising p-type transparent conductors, showing that the Cu-based chemical modulation of the valence band rule can be generalized beyond oxides to halide systems.
engineering_relevance: These materials could enable more practical transparent electrodes for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics by combining optical transparency with intrinsic p-type conductivity.
method: Minima hopping method to explore X–Cu–I compound structures
Density functional theory screening for stability, band gap, and hole effective mass
Applied CMVB design-rule analysis to the resulting candidate set
evidence_signal: The screening yielded 58 candidates, including 49 previously unreported compounds and 20 p-type degenerate semiconductors; Cu2FI2 was highlighted with a 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m0 hole effective mass.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, and defect behavior still need validation before device integration.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
